'''George Rushing Kempf''' ([[Globe, Arizona]], August 12, 1944 – [[Lawrence, Kansas]], July 16, 2002) was a mathematician who worked on [[algebraic geometry]], who proved the [[Riemann–Kempf singularity theorem]], the [[Kempf–Ness theorem]], the [[Kempf vanishing theorem]], and who introduced [[Kempf variety|Kempf varieties]].

==Mumford on Kempf==
'I met George in 1970 when he burst on the algebraic geometry scene with a spectacular PhD thesis. His thesis gave a wonderful analysis of the singularities of the subvarieties <math>W_r</math> of the Jacobian of a curve obtained by adding the curve to itself <math>r</math> times inside its Jacobian. This was one of the major themes that he pursued throughout his career: understanding the interaction of a curve with its Jacobian and especially to the map from the <math>r</math>-fold symmetric product of the curve to the Jacobian. In his thesis he gave a determinantal representation both of <math>W_r</math> and of its tangent cone at all its singular points, which gives you a complete understanding of the nature of these singularities' – [[David Mumford]]<ref name=mumford>{{Citation | last1=Mumford | first1=David | author1-link=David Mumford | title=In memoriam: George R. Kempf 1944–2002 | url=http://muse.jhu.edu/journals/american_journal_of_mathematics/v124/124.6mumford.pdf |mr=1939780 | year=2002 | journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] | issn=0002-9327 | volume=124 | issue=6 | pages=iii–iv | doi=10.1353/ajm.2002.0040| s2cid=120437883 }}</ref>

'One of the things that distinguished his work was the total mastery with which he used higher cohomology. A paper which, I believe, every new student of algebraic geometry should read, is his elementary proof of the Riemann-Roch theorem on curves: “Algebraic Curves” in Crelle, 1977. That such an old result could be treated with new insight was the work of a master.' – David Mumford<ref name=mumford/>
